item.title: Singapore breaks ground on low-carbon testbed and announces first industry users
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Singapore on Friday broke ground on the S$62.5 million ($48.92 million) Low-Carbon Technology Translational Testbed (LCT), a national facility that will help companies test and scale emerging low-carbon technologies for industrial use.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore on Friday broke ground on the S$62.5 million ($48.92 million) Low-Carbon Technology Translational Testbed (LCT), a national facility that will help companies test and scale emerging low-carbon technologies for industrial use.

Amogy, IHI Corporation, and Metha8 were announced as its first users, through collaborations spanning carbon utilisation and low-carbon hydrogen, The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) said in a statement.

It is noted that industrial activities, including manufacturing, account for nearly two-thirds of Singapore’s emissions.

Reducing these emissions will require technologies suited to Singapore’s industrial conditions and facilities to test them at larger scale.

Located on Jurong Island and hosted at the A*STAR Institute of Sustainability for Chemicals, Energy and Environment (A*STAR ISCE), LCT will provide modular and configurable facilities to support the development and testing of carbon utilisation and hydrogen technologies under industry-relevant conditions.

Companies can access shared infrastructure, utilities, permits and licences to set up pilots, moving faster from technology development to testing and scale-up.

It complements JTC’s broader efforts to develop the island as a leading hub for new energy solutions and low-carbon technologies.

According to the statement, A*STAR and Amogy will pilot ammonia-to-hydrogen technology at LCT, developing lower-cost catalysts and integrating Amogy’s ammonia cracking systems to produce up to one tonne of hydrogen per day.

The project will support the commercialization of new non-noble metal catalysts and generate operating data for the larger-scale deployment of ammonia-based hydrogen and power across Singapore’s industrial and energy sectors.

Meanwhile, A*STAR and IHI Corporation will test carbon dioxide (CO₂)-to-Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) catalyst technologies at LCT.

The partners will evaluate catalyst performance under industrially relevant conditions, including industrial flow rates, temperatures and pressures, real-world feedstocks, and extended operating durations.

The data generated will provide valuable insights into catalyst activity, selectivity, stability and scalability, supporting IHI’s efforts to advance the technology towards commercial deployment.

A*STAR and Singapore-based start-up Metha8 will scale up an integrated methanol-to-power system.

It produces hydrogen through an aqueous alkaline methanol reforming process, while simultaneously capturing pure CO2 as a by-product prior to power generation.

Testing at LCT will validate its viability under industrially relevant operating conditions and generate the operational data required to support future scale-up and deployment.

Beyond these first industry projects, A*STAR is developing collaborations with local and international technology developers, energy companies and industrial partners to test and advance low-carbon technologies at LCT.

These include CERT Systems, Greenlyzer, Obayashi, and RTI International.

“Jurong Island brings together companies with significant industrial decarbonisation needs and a growing base of technology and research capabilities,

“LCT builds on these strengths by giving companies a plug-and-play platform to develop and validate promising technologies for future scale-up and deployment,” said Lim Wey-Len, Executive Vice President, EDB.

Professor Lim Keng Hui, Assistant Chief Executive Officer, Science & Engineering Research Council, A*STAR, said promising technologies that work in the lab must still prove they can operate reliably under demanding industrial conditions.

“LCT gives researchers and companies the infrastructure and operating environment to do this without building a facility from scratch. With construction underway and our first collaborations in place, we can work with industry to identify which low-carbon solutions can scale for Singapore and beyond,” he added.

item.title: Singapore-founded AnyMind enters the U.S. market
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: AnyMind Group, a business-process-as-a-service (BPaaS) company for marketing, e-commerce and digital transformation, has on Thursday announced the launch of operations in the United States of America, and will operate out of Los Angeles, California.
item.content:encoded:
AnyMind Group, a business-process-as-a-service (BPaaS) company for marketing, e-commerce and digital transformation, has on Thursday announced the launch of operations in the United States of America, and will operate out of Los Angeles, California.

The expansion marks another step in the company’s vision to “build the world’s new gen business infrastructure” by providing businesses in the U.S. with access to its end-to-end solutions spanning proprietary technology, in-market operations and partner networks, and overseas businesses with the building blocks to enter the U.S. market, the firm said in a statement.

AnyMind Group’s expansion into the U.S. is intended to extend in-market support and integrations for businesses in Asia-Pacific that are looking to enter the U.S. market, and for U.S.-based companies to leverage AnyMind Group’s proprietary technology for domestic growth and to expand across Asia-Pacific through the company’s existing range of solutions spanning marketing, commerce, logistics and distribution.

The launch builds on existing client activity. Over the past seven months, AnyMind Group has supported 15 Asian brands with their expansion and growth in the U.S. Establishing a local presence will enable the company to deepen this support and develop its U.S. partner network.

For the U.S. market, the company will first roll out its live commerce platform, AnyLive and its data and AI utilization solution suite that includes enterprise-grade agentic AI, online/offline retail data unification and utilization, AIGC (AI-Generated Content), brand and consumer analytics, and more.

AnyMind Group combines proprietary software with in-market operations teams – in a BPaaS model – to help businesses generate demand, sell products and manage the processes behind their growth.

Its capabilities span influencer marketing and digital advertising, live and social commerce, e-commerce management, customer engagement, logistics, offline distribution, and AI and data utilization.

Through this integrated approach, clients can connect marketing with sales and fulfillment, supported by teams that understand each market’s consumers, commercial channels and operating requirements.

“Our immediate priority is to respond to the client demand we are already seeing and turn that demand into tangible results. Building a local team and partner network will help us understand the U.S. market and support our clients’ long-term growth,

“By connecting the expertise and networks we develop in the U.S. with our existing infrastructure across Asia-Pacific, we can help businesses grow in both directions. This will create new opportunities for our clients and strengthen the value we deliver across markets,” said Kosuke Sogo, Chief Executive Officer, AnyMind Group.

Founded in Singapore in 2016, AnyMind Group established a presence in 15 markets across Southeast Asia, East Asia, India, and the Middle East before entering the U.S., and serves over 1,500 APAC and international enterprises for marketing, 230 enterprises for commerce, 1,600 publishers, and 1,100 creators as of June 2026.

The company moved its headquarters to Tokyo, Japan, in 2019 and went public on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth Market in 2023.

item.title: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand central banks join BLOOM to advance cross-border digital money settlement
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Bank of Thailand (BOT) have joined its BLOOM initiative as policymaker members.
item.content:encoded:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Bank of Thailand (BOT) have joined its BLOOM initiative as policymaker members.

In a statement on Friday, the MAS said the three central banks will work with industry players to develop common approaches to cross-border use of digital money. The cooperation includes acceptance of different digital money, exchanged and settled across institutions, networks, and jurisdictions.

Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online and Multi-currency (BLOOM) is a public-private initiative that brings together policymakers, financial institutions, payment networks, and technology providers.

MAS said greater coordination will be needed as financial institutions and jurisdictions develop different digital money uses, including tokenised deposits and regulated stablecoins.

The initiative aims to deepen engagement between policymakers and industry on settlement infrastructure and on frameworks that promote interoperability. It will consider how international standards and jurisdiction-specific supervisory expectations can apply to cross-border transactions, while allowing for differences in local requirements.

BLOOM’s participation has also expanded to include Airwallex, Mastercard, Maybank, Monee, Nium, Ripple, ShopeePay, Visa, and the World Bank Group.

MAS said participants are advancing digital money applications in payments, treasury and trade finance, including tokenised deposits, regulated stablecoins and settlement across payment networks.

The World Bank Group’s participation as a multilateral development bank will bring its experience in payment systems modernization, cross-border payments, and financial inclusion, including the perspectives of developing economies.

Participants will focus on three areas. The first is acceptance and settlement across jurisdictions, including how financial institutions accept different forms of digital money, how counterparties contract with one another, and how transactions settle across markets.

The second is interoperability, pushing different digital money arrangements to operate across networks, infrastructure, and borders.

The third is programmable controls, such as identity verification, sanctions screening, and transaction limits.

MAS said BLOOM would reduce the need for financial institutions to set up separate arrangements with each counterparty or market, which would lower implementation costs and speed time to market.

Leong Sing Chiong, deputy managing director for markets and development at MAS, said the future of finance will involve multiple forms of digital money. Collaboration between policymakers and industry will be needed to address acceptance, settlement, and interoperability.

Aznan bin Abdul Aziz, deputy governor of BNM, said a future in which cross-border payments can be made using multiple forms of digital money is closer to reality than it was, and that BNM looks forward to exploring it through BLOOM with the participating central banks and industry partners.

Daranee Saeju, deputy governor for payment systems stability and financial services supervision at BOT, said the bank welcomes the chance to help inform forward-looking regulatory approaches for tokenised money, particularly in cross-border payments and wholesale settlement, while keeping oversight prudent and proportionate.

Maybank Singapore, one of the new participants, said in August that it aims to help shape common standards and infrastructure for digital finance in Singapore.

UK and Singapore deepen cooperation on digital finance and sustainable finance

item.title: Danantara CIO Pandu Sjahrir says Indonesian corporate fundamentals remain strong despite market concerns
item.dc:creator: Yimie Yong
item.description: The investment chief cites 15 percent first-half profit growth among major listed companies as Indonesia pushes ahead with capital market reforms.
item.content:encoded:
Indonesian companies continue to demonstrate strong business fundamentals despite mounting concerns over the country’s capital market governance, sovereign fund Danantara Indonesia CIO Pandu Sjahrir said, urging investors to distinguish between market integrity issues and corporate performance.

In a LinkedIn post on Friday, Pandu said Indonesia’s capital market reforms were necessary to build a more transparent, fair and trusted market, while stressing that the strength of listed companies should be assessed objectively.

His remarks came as Indonesia faces renewed scrutiny from global index provider MSCI over market transparency and investability, raising concerns about the country’s standing in international equity benchmarks. Pandu said the concerns should be taken seriously, given their potential impact on the country’s 32 million capital market investors.

“At the same time, we need to distinguish between issues of market governance and the fundamentals of companies.” he wrote in the post.

“The market should be fixed, by all means, but the business strength of Indonesian companies should still be assessed objectively,” he added.

Pandu cited data showing that 134 of 146 listed companies with annual revenue exceeding IDR 5 trillion ($276 million) recorded profits. Their aggregate profits grew 15 percent in the first half of 2026 from a year earlier, while revenue increased 7 percent.

Meanwhile, 121 non-financial issuers held a combined IDR 583 trillion in cash in the second quarter of 2026, up 13 percent year on year, providing capacity to finance business expansion.

He also pointed to opportunities among companies trading at valuations he described as attractive. Of the 146 companies, 61 recorded return on equity above 15 percent. Some businesses in the banking and consumer sectors generated returns on equity of around 20 percent while trading at price-to-earnings ratios below 10 times.

Pandu said investors should assess companies based on their profitability, business growth, cash flow, debt levels and corporate governance, rather than assuming that falling share prices automatically make stocks cheap.

FTSE Russell, meanwhile, retained Indonesia’s classification as a Secondary Emerging Market, while continuing to monitor the implementation and effectiveness of the reforms.

Pandu also expressed support for the reform efforts led by Indonesia’s Financial Services Authority (OJK), the Indonesia Stock Exchange, Bank Indonesia and the Ministry of Finance, alongside other stakeholders.

“Ultimately, capital market reform will not be completed overnight, but it must be consistent and deliver visible results,” he said.

Pandu advised investors to stay optimistic while remaining disciplined, understanding the businesses they invest in, diversifying their portfolios and matching investments to their individual risk profiles.

He said Indonesia was moving in a better direction, although further work remained to restore confidence and strengthen the capital market.

GIC, Temasek reject claims of pressuring MSCI over Indonesia downgrade – report

item.title: Singapore picks Keppel, Sembcorp, Tuas Power for Southeast Asia’s first biomethane import pilot
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) has appointed three power generators, Keppel Energy, Sembcorp Utilities, and Tuas Power Generation, as biomethane aggregators under Singapore's 300-MW regulatory sandbox.
item.content:encoded:
The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) has appointed three power generators, Keppel Energy, Sembcorp Utilities, and Tuas Power Generation, as biomethane aggregators under Singapore’s 300-MW regulatory sandbox.

In a statement on Friday, the Singapore EDB said said the program, also the first of its kind in Southeast Asia, will import and supply biomethane, a renewable alternative to natural gas.

The 15-year sandbox will test the commercial, regulatory, and operational arrangements needed to import biomethane, EDB said. The aim is to shape the frameworks for wider adoption.

The pilot plan is expected to bring in the first supplies by the end of 2028. Under the sandbox, the three companies will import up to 300 MW of biomethane from regional and international sources.

They will supply it to data centers and industrial manufacturers in Singapore, either as gas or as electricity generated from it. The EDB said the capacity could meet the annual energy needs of about 600,000 Housing and Development Board households.

The EDB said biomethane can be used as a direct replacement for natural gas, using existing gas infrastructure and equipment without modification.

The EDB said natural gas makes up about 95 percent of Singapore’s electricity generation, so biomethane offers a feasible way to cut emissions from the power sector and from gas-dependent industries.

Beyond emissions, the EDB said the sandbox would strengthen energy security by diversifying Singapore’s gas supply beyond conventional natural gas. It said the sandbox would also help build supply chains, commercial models, and sustainability standards for wider deployment.

Lim Wey-Len, executive vice president of the EDB, said the sandbox is an important pilot for discovering new decarbonization pathways for the manufacturing and data center sectors.

item.title: Singapore launches S$143M industrial decarbonisation funding
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Singapore has launched a S$143 million ($112 million) funding initiative to speed up the development and commercialization of low-carbon technologies for industry.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore has launched a S$143 million ($112 million) funding initiative to speed up the development and commercialization of low-carbon technologies for industry.

In a statement on Friday, the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) said the fund includes up to S$100 million set aside for company-led research and development.

This is the largest single funding initiative dedicated to industrial decarbonization research to date. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry Gan Kim Yong announced it at the inaugural Singapore Industry Decarbonisation Forum 2026, alongside new partnerships with climate and clean-energy investors.

Industry, including manufacturing, accounts for nearly two-thirds of Singapore’s emissions, the government said. Emissions from energy-intensive activities such as petrochemicals, refining, and fuel combustion, are difficult to cut.

Meanwhile, Singapore’s limited land and resources restrict the deployment of some solutions at scale. Targeted research is needed to adapt technologies to Singapore’s conditions, the government added.

The S$143 million Industry Decarbonisation Funding Initiative, led by the Economic Development Board (EDB) and the Advanced Energy and Decarbonisation Office (AEDO), will fund research into three areas.

The first is carbon capture, to develop cost-effective ways to capture carbon dioxide from low- and mid-concentration streams.

The second is carbon utilization, converting captured carbon dioxide into chemicals and other products, drawing on Singapore’s energy and chemicals ecosystem.

The third covers other emerging technologies, including carbon storage, electrification of industrial heating, and reducing non-carbon dioxide greenhouse gases from industrial processes such as semiconductor manufacturing.

The initiative is part of the S$800 million Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 Decarbonisation Grand Challenge. Low-carbon hydrogen research will continue under the broader challenge, focusing on lowering the cost and land needs of hydrogen use.

The government said the initiative will feed promising technologies into scale-up programs, including the Low-Carbon Technology Translational Testbed and the Singapore Pilots for Energy and Enterprise Decarbonisation program.

Up to S$100 million of the initiative is set aside for a new Decarbonisation Research for Industry, Ventures and Enterprise (DRIVE) program. Under DRIVE, companies, including start-ups and technology providers, can propose and design research projects with Singapore’s public research institutions. The government will co-fund up to 75 percent of qualifying project costs.

Jermaine Loy, managing director of EDB, said decarbonization is essential to keeping Singapore’s manufacturing competitive. The initiative can bring companies and researchers together to tackle industrial challenges.

The government also announced partnerships that EDB and AEDO have set up with Extantia, Main Sequence and the Rocky Mountain Institute. These join existing collaborations with Breakthrough Energy, Energy Impact Partners, SG Growth Capital, and Temasek. The partners will share views on emerging technologies and industry needs, and recommend companies for Singapore’s decarbonization initiatives.

On the same day, TotalEnergies signed a memorandum of understanding with the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)’s Institute of Sustainability for Chemicals, Energy and Environment to explore research on carbon utilization technologies.

AEDO has also awarded S$65 million under its Low Carbon Energy Research Scale-up Grant to five projects that delivered promising results under an earlier program. The teams will receive follow-on funding to scale their technologies in industrial settings.

US-based Energy Impact Partners to jointly scale Singapore decarbonisation startups

item.title: US-based Energy Impact Partners to jointly scale Singapore decarbonisation startups
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Energy Impact Partners (EIP), a global energy investor, and the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) will boost their partnership to advance energy innovation and decarbonisation in Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Energy Impact Partners (EIP), a global energy investor, and the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) will boost their partnership to advance energy innovation and decarbonisation in Singapore.

In a statement on Friday, New York-based EIP said the two made the announcement at the inaugural Singapore Industry Decarbonisation Forum 2026. The EDB jointly hosted the event with the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) and the Advanced Energy and Decarbonisation Office.

Singapore’s research base, industrial infrastructure, and regional connectivity can complement EIP’s global reach, such as energy-industrial companies and startups. They can support the full innovation path, from research and development and test-bedding to scale-up and commercial deployment.

Under the expanded partnership, EIP will connect promising companies to Singapore’s innovation landscape and open channels for technical exchange and strategic collaboration. They will also deepen ties between their networks and look at ways to commercialize and scale new technologies.

The partnership supports Singapore’s Decarbonisation Grand Challenge by creating pathways for companies to develop and scale from Singapore.

Anil Achyuta, partner for frontier investments at EIP, said the partnership reflects Singapore’s ambition in the energy transition. Connecting EDB’s ecosystem with EIP’s global network can help promising energy startups find a path to scale in Singapore and beyond.

Wey-Len Lim, executive vice president at EDB, said partnerships with global investors like EIP help Singapore learn about emerging technologies and industry needs. The partnership would connect technology companies with Singapore’s research and industry ecosystem to develop and scale solutions for the country’s decarbonisation needs.

Singapore launches new coalition to mobilize demand, financing for carbon credits

item.title: Singapore’s Boroo to buy Canada’s Eagle gold mine for C$140M
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Boroo, a privately held investment holding company based in Singapore, has signed an agreement to acquire Victoria Gold Corp., whose main asset is the Eagle Gold Mine in Canada, for C$140 million ($100 million).
item.content:encoded:
Boroo, a privately held investment holding company based in Singapore, has signed an agreement to acquire Victoria Gold Corp., whose main asset is the Eagle Gold Mine in Canada, for C$140 million ($100 million).

In a statement on Friday, Boroo said the buyer is Boroo’s subsidiary Gatsuurt Mining Inc. The deal is subject to approval from the Ontario Superior Court of Justice. The receiver intends to seek court approval in early December 2026 and aims to close around December 31, 2026.

Boroo also said the deal is also subject to clearance under Canada’s Competition Act and to the Yukon government’s consent as receivership lender.

Victoria Gold was placed into receivership in August 2024, after a landslide at the mine’s heap leach pad released millions of tonnes of ore and at least 280,000 cubic meters of cyanide-containing solution beyond containment in June 2024. The mine is about 375 kilometers north of Whitehorse, in the traditional territory of the First Nation of Na-Cho Nyäk Dun.

The acquisition would include the Eagle Gold Mine, certain Victoria Gold subsidiaries, a set of mineral claims in the Dublin Gulch and Victoria Block West areas, the Olive Crown Grant and certain contracts.

Boroo said it plans to spend about C$800 million between 2027 and 2029 on environmental rehabilitation, water treatment, geotechnical stabilization, and a phased restart.

The company said it expects to commit more than C$1.5 billion in Canada overall. Boroo said these investments could provide stable, skilled jobs for Yukoners, and contracting opportunities for the First Nation.

item.title: Google Cloud to offer OpenAI models through Model Garden
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Google Cloud is adding OpenAI models and Codex workflows to its enterprise AI platform, initially in private preview, with wider availability planned in the coming weeks.
item.content:encoded:
Google Cloud will add OpenAI’s latest AI models to its Model Garden platform, allowing enterprise customers to access them through Google Cloud’s existing infrastructure, governance controls and commercial agreements.

The companies announced the arrangement on October 21. The initial lineup includes GPT-Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. According to Google Cloud’s announcement, the models are rolling out in private preview to selected enterprise customers, with broader access planned in the coming weeks.

Customers will be able to purchase usage through Google Cloud Marketplace and apply existing cloud spending commitments. The integration adds OpenAI models to a platform that already offers more than 200 models from Google, third-party developers and open-model providers.

Enterprise access and controls

The arrangement is aimed at companies developing AI agents and other production workloads that need to compare models by capability, price and response time. Google Cloud says customers can select among models without establishing a separate procurement arrangement for every provider.

It also plans to support local Codex command-line and desktop workflows through the cloud platform. Further integrations with Gemini for business and Google Antigravity are forthcoming, the companies said.

Google Cloud said its access controls, centralized audit logging and network boundaries will apply to OpenAI workloads deployed through the service. It said customer prompts and outputs would remain within designated data perimeters and would not be used to train foundation models. Zero Data Retention options and Confidential Compute support are planned rather than generally available at launch.

Those distinctions will be relevant for enterprises deciding whether a preview release meets their regulatory and internal security requirements. Organizations will still need to assess regional service availability, the treatment of sensitive information and the contractual scope of the available controls.

Cloud AI competition widens

By adding OpenAI models alongside its own Gemini family and other providers, Google Cloud is positioning Model Garden as a place for businesses to manage different AI workloads on one platform. The companies have not disclosed customer uptake, regional rollout dates or pricing for each model in this announcement.

The partnership gives organizations another route to OpenAI models at a time when technology buyers are weighing the cost of deploying AI agents, the need for model flexibility and the difficulty of governing automated access to company systems.

Read the companies’ OpenAI announcement for additional integration details.

Blueprint Alliance formed by Okta, AWS, Google Cloud and others for AI-agent security

item.title: AI-related job ads in Singapore more than triple, Jobstreet study finds
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: The share of Singapore job ads mentioning AI-related skills rose from 1.3 percent in January 2024 to 5.1 percent in August 2026, according to Jobstreet by SEEK.
item.content:encoded:
The share of job advertisements in Singapore mentioning artificial intelligence skills rose from 1.3 percent in January 2024 to 5.1 percent in August 2026, according to a new analysis from Jobstreet by SEEK.

The figures come from the employment platform’s AI Gauge, which examines references to AI skills in job advertisements across eight Asia Pacific markets. Singapore had the third-highest proportion of AI-related listings in the analysis, behind Hong Kong at 6.6 percent and Thailand at 5.2 percent.

The increase suggests that employers are seeking AI capabilities across a wider range of occupations. The numbers describe advertised requirements on SEEK’s platforms, rather than the number of people hired into AI roles or a measure of the entire labor market.

Demand spreads beyond technical roles

Machine learning remained the most commonly mentioned AI skill in Singapore job ads, Jobstreet said. Listings referring to machine learning increased 93 percent in the three months through August 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier, the fastest growth among markets the company studied.

Mentions of agentic AI-related terms rose by 460 percent between August 2025 and August 2026. That is a year-on-year change in advertisements containing those terms; the company did not provide the underlying count in its media summary, which makes the size of the initial base important when interpreting the growth rate.

The share of information and communications technology job advertisements referencing AI-related terms increased from an average of 7.2 percent in the six months through August 2024 to 21.3 percent in the comparable six-month period through August 2026.

Outside the technology sector, the share in advertising, arts and media rose from 2.3 percent to 10.2 percent, according to the analysis.

How job descriptions are changing

The types of positions requiring AI knowledge also appear to be changing. In 2024, job titles commonly associated with the skills included data scientist, software engineer and software developer. By 2026, AI engineer and automation engineer appeared alongside software engineer among the most frequent titles.

The report distinguishes everyday familiarity with generative AI tools from more specialized technical, governance and operational experience. Employers may need to be clearer about those differences when specifying job requirements and assessing candidates.

The findings follow Singapore government data indicating that technology employment and AI skills demand are expanding. SEEK’s findings add a regional perspective to the changing mix of roles and skills associated with AI adoption. They do not establish how many positions have been filled, whether wages have increased or how much AI has raised productivity in the businesses advertising those vacancies.

Singapore’s digital economy reaches 19.3% of GDP as AI adoption deepens: IMDA
